subject: PO requirements and invoice cadence for enterprise commitment
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medpulse.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@medpulse.com
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO template + invoice cadence requirements for Redwood deployment

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — MedPulse is excited to move the Redwood deployment into procurement. Our legal & AP teams have two constraints we need you to confirm:

1) Purchase order mapping: our ERP requires a PO number on each invoice and we must attach a PO line per billing item. We can issue an umbrella PO for the program but need a BU-level reference on each invoice line so our ERP can auto-post.

2) Invoice cadence & net terms: our default is weekly invoices with Net60 payment terms. That cadence is driven by internal cashflow and monthly reconciliation windows.

3) Discount eligibility: discounts in our pricing matrix are applied only when we receive consolidated monthly statements. If you require monthly invoices to grant a volume discount, please state that explicitly.

I attached the PO draft (MedPulse_PO_2026-09.pdf) and the SOW outline. Can Redwood accept: (a) umbrella PO + BU line mapping on invoice, (b) weekly invoices, Net60? If not, what alternatives would you propose and how would that affect pricing?

Best,
Tara
Procurement Manager, MedPulse
Attachments: MedPulse_PO_2026-09.pdf (application/pdf)

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medpulse.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO template + invoice cadence requirements for Redwood deployment

Tara — thanks for sending this over and for the clear requirements. A few quick points to clarify from Redwood's side: 

- We can accept an umbrella PO, and we can include BU-level reference fields on each invoice line (we typically map to an "internal_reference" field). We'll need the exact BU codes you use so our billing system writes them to the correct line items.

- Standard Redwood hosted billing is consolidated monthly statements with Net45. Weekly invoices are unusual for us operationally because they increase our AR processing and reduce our ability to offer volume-based discounts.

- Pricing/discounts: our published volume discount tiers are applied at the statement level. If MedPulse requires weekly invoices, we will need to evaluate how discounts are calculated (per-week vs consolidated). In practice we can offer either: 
  * Option A — Consolidated monthly invoices + standard tiered discounts (preferred)
  * Option B — Bi-weekly or weekly invoices, with discounts converted to fixed credit tiers (smaller effective discount)

I looped in Vanessa (account lead) and Sean (billing) to confirm the financial tradeoffs and any operational changes. Can you confirm the BU codes and whether your AP team has flexibility to accept bi-weekly or a monthly consolidated statement for discounting?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: internal: MedPulse PO cadence — pricing options

Quick note — tagging here so we have an internal record while we wait for Tara's BU codes: 

- If MedPulse accepts monthly consolidated statements + Net45, we can offer the standard volume discount band: 8% at $250k+/month, 12% at $500k+. That preserves margins and keeps finance happy.

- If they insist on weekly invoices & Net60, ask Sean for a proposal on a fixed-credit approach. My thinking: convert the 8% into a 3% weekly credit applied at invoice level (effectively lower than consolidated discount) or hold a preauth reconciliation monthly where we apply a one-time usage credit.

- Operational impact: weekly invoicing requires an ERP mapping run and increases our AP_workload. We should request a 3-month pilot and a small implementation fee ($1,500) to do the invoice mapping and automation.

Sean — can you draft the credit/fee numbers and confirm any ARR impact? I want to present a clean tradeoff instead of a binary yes/no.

— Vanessa
Account Executive

From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medpulse.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@medpulse.com
Date: 2026-09-29T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO template + invoice cadence requirements for Redwood deployment

Irene — appreciate the quick reply. MedPulse can be flexible but has internal constraints: weekly runs are preferred during our rollout months; after stabilization we could move to monthly consolidations. Two potential compromises: 

1) Bi-weekly invoices (every other Friday) + Net50 for the first 90 days, then transition to monthly Net45 if we hit adoption thresholds.
2) Umbrella PO accepted, but we need the BU code per line item. We can provide a mapping table.

Regarding discounts: if Redwood requires monthly consolidation to apply the tiers, please provide the alternate credit structure you mentioned (convert 8% to a per-invoice credit). We'll evaluate internally but will likely prefer a bi-weekly cadence if the effective discount remains within ~150–200 bps of your monthly tier.

If you can produce a short sample invoice that demonstrates how BU codes will appear and a draft credit calculation for bi-weekly vs monthly, we can speed approvals.

Thanks,
Tara

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medpulse.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO template + invoice cadence requirements for Redwood deployment

Tara — thanks, this is helpful. Proposal from Redwood: 

1) Pilot: 90-day bi-weekly invoice cadence, Net50. During pilot we will apply an "interim credit" on each bi-weekly invoice equivalent to 6% annualized (roughly ~3% effective gap vs our 8% monthly band). After 90 days, if usage meets the agreed thresholds, we switch to consolidated monthly billing with full volume discounts and Net45.

2) PO mapping: we can accept the umbrella PO and will write BU codes to invoice line-level fields. Please send the BU mapping CSV and we will validate it against our billing system. Implementation includes a one-time mapping setup fee of $1,250 (covers engineering & AP configuration).

3) Contracts: I'll attach the updated SOW (Redwood_SOW_v2.docx) with a short amendment describing the pilot cadence and the credit reconciliation approach. Legal will draft a short amendment to the MSA to make this binding.

If that structure works, Vanessa will prepare the commercial amendment and Sean will produce a sample bi-weekly invoice for your AP to review. Next steps: Tara to send BU codes + confirm approval to proceed with a 3-month pilot.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
